title: Native classes without assigned icons in the "Inherited By" or "Inherits" sections do not show their base class' icon in the class reference doc
body: ### Tested versions master [2f2a9f4cc6ecba0d802c5f4ca46f0d6d4d88a18b] v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] ### System information Godot v4.8.dev (2f2a9f4cc6ecba0d802c5f4ca46f0d6d4d88a18b) - macOS Sequoia (15.7.5) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 (Apple9) - Apple M4 (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description I couldn't find an equivalent issue, but if there is, feel free to close this one as duplicate. `EditorSyntaxHighlighter` does not have an icon assigned to it (like there's no `editor/icons/EditorSyntaxHighlighter.svg` file). Therefore it should inherit from the base class like it does here in the class reference help search: But it does not. Also see here: I don't think this is a regression because it was like that in `4.6` too, just without an icon at all (You can also see how `Resource` and `RefCounted` don't show an icon either): This only applies to native classes. User classes are shown correctly (after a cache clear ofc): It became glaringly obvious here (which was how I discovered this): A workaround is to duplicate the icon and rename it to each subclass, but that's unwieldy and unwanted, ofc. I'm not sure whether this is a _bug_ or just an oversight, but I posted this issue in the main repo because it seems like unexpected behavior, considering it shows up correctly in the help search and elsewhere (including the next to the doc title itself), and user classes' behavior is expected. Of course, this doesn't apply to most classes, but as discussed in godotengine/godot-proposals#15336, making an icon for every subclass takes a while, so I think this should be fixed at least. ### Steps to reproduce On any `4.x` version, search up "Syntax" in the class reference help search to find it easily. You can also check out `PanelContainer` (both subclasses don't have assigned icons), `Texture2D` (two subclasses don't have assigned icons), or `InputEvent` (a few descendant classes don't have them). You can also make a script extend those subclasses and a script extend that user class to see that user classes show their icon in the docs for comparison. (`AudioEffect`'s icon was added after `4.8.dev3`, so previous versions show the default icon/no icon in the docs.) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
